diagnostic_evidence.quote: Let $c$ be a cost function such that for all particle $i$, $c_i : y\in \Omega \mapsto c(y,\bm{x}_i)\in [0,+\infty) $ belongs to $C^{1,1}(\Omega)$.
On the contrary, when $\alpha<1$, the cost is a concave function of the distance, which allows larger deformations and potentially shapes far from the base ball shape.
and a power cost $c(\bm{x},\bm{x}_i) = |\bm{x}-\bm{x}_i|^{\alpha_i}$ where the $\alpha_i$ are distributed uniformly between 0.5 and 4
Theorem~\ref{thm:semidiscrete} shows that for any such configuration, there is always a unique partition of the space that satisfies the volume constraint.

issues.failure_explanation: The sole hypothesis (each c_i in C^{1,1}(Omega)) does not support the conclusion. Counterexample within the stated hypotheses: a cost independent of the target, c(x,y)=|x|^2, is C^{1,1}; then the objective of (eq:Monge) equals the integral of |x|^2 over Omega for every volume-constrained partition, so the Monge problem has infinitely many solutions, and the sets of (eq:Laguerre) collapse to at most one nonempty cell ({c_i - w_i <= c_j - w_j forall j} holds identically for the maximal weight), so no weights satisfy |L_i| = v_i for N >= 2 with all v_i > 0, and 'the intersection of two Laguerre cells has zero Lebesgue measure' also fails. Coincident seeds give the same failure. Moreover, the theorem is applied to the paper's flagship costs which violate even the stated hypothesis: c = lambda^{-1}|y-x_i|^alpha is not C^{1,1} on Omega whenever the seed x_i lies in Omega and alpha < 2 (the gradient alpha*|y-x_i|^{alpha-2}(y-x_i) is not Lipschitz at y=x_i and is undefined there for alpha <= 1), while the paper's soft-particle regime uses exactly alpha in {0.5, 0.75, 1} and alpha_i uniform in [0.5, 4]; the level-set cost (eq:costshape) likewise fails C^{1,1} for hardness p < 2. Hence the uniqueness-and-volume guarantee is unproven (and in degenerate cases false) in the regimes where the model is advertised.

failure_location.quote: Then the Monge problem \eqref{eq:Monge} has a unique solution $T$ given by

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restate the theorem under the hypotheses actually used in the cited proofs (twist-type/nondegeneracy condition on c and distinct atoms, or strictly convex superlinear costs), and weaken the prose so uniqueness is claimed only for those regimes, noting that the concave soft costs and general shape costs are covered only numerically or under additional genericity assumptions.
issues.overall_effect: The guarantee that 'for any such configuration, there is always a unique partition of the space that satisfies the volume constraint' (used to justify the dynamical scheme and the incompressibility force) is unsupported: the theorem is false as stated under its own hypotheses, and no valid substitute is established for the soft (alpha < 2) power costs, the arbitrary level-set costs, or the periodized costs used in the experiments. The numerical solver and the experiments do not depend on uniqueness, so they survive.
issues.title: Semi-discrete uniqueness theorem stated under insufficient hypotheses and applied outside them
issues.why_classification: The supported repair is a contained restatement of hypotheses plus a limited weakening of the advertised 'arbitrary cost' scope; the tessellation method, the solver and all numerical guarantees survive. It exceeds a routine local fix because a substantive promised regime (uniqueness for arbitrary/soft costs) must be withdrawn or newly argued, but no new global proof architecture is needed.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: return as output the unique vector of optimal values for the Kantorovitch potentials $(w_1, \dots, w_N)$.

issues.failure_explanation: The Laguerre cells depend on the potentials only through the differences w_i - w_j, so for any solution w the vector w + t(1,...,1) is another solution with identical cells and identical volumes for every real t. The weights are therefore determined only up to an additive constant (a gauge such as sum_i v_i w_i = 0 must be fixed); the theorem's assertion that they 'are uniquely defined', repeated in the claim that solvers 'return as output the unique vector of optimal values', is false as written. The cited semi-discrete theory yields uniqueness at most modulo this gauge.

failure_location.quote: the weights $w_i\in \mathbb{R}$, called Kantorovich potentials, are uniquely defined such that for all $i\in\{1,\ldots,N\}$,

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add 'up to the addition of a common constant' (or fix a gauge such as sum_i v_i w_i = 0) in the theorem and in the sentence describing solver outputs.
issues.overall_effect: The uniqueness assertion about the potentials, in the theorem and in the description of optimal transport solvers, is incorrect as stated; the tessellation itself, the volume constraints and every downstream result are unaffected because they depend only on the gauge-invariant cells.
issues.title: Kantorovich potentials claimed unique although defined only up to an additive constant
issues.why_classification: A one-line qualification (or fixing a gauge) fully restores the statement; no substantive claim, construction or guarantee changes, since the cells and volumes are gauge-invariant.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: First of all, since the function $U : w \mapsto |\mathscr{S}(w)|$ is non-decreasing, $U(0)=0$ and $U(w)\to1$ as $w\to+\infty$ there exists a unique $w^*>0$ such that $U(w^*) = v_i$.
Then let $\mathscr{S}\subset\Omega$ be any shape of volume $v_i$.
Consequently, any particle shape can be realized using an appropriate cost function $c_i : \bm{x}\in \Omega \mapsto c(\bm{x},\bm{x}_i)\in [0,+\infty) $.

issues.failure_explanation: A non-decreasing function need not attain intermediate values: U(w)=|{c <= w}| is non-decreasing and can jump over v_i whenever the cost has a level set of positive measure, which the framework permits since costs are arbitrary nonnegative functions (the medium particle even uses c identically 0). Concrete counterexample inside the paper's own cost class: c(x,x_i) = (max(0,|x-x_i|-R_0))^2 is C^{1,1} and nonnegative with {c <= 0} = B(x_i,R_0) of positive volume, so U jumps at w = 0 from 0 to |B(x_i,R_0)|; for any target volume v_i < |B| no w* exists, and the actual minimizers of I over sets of volume v_i are arbitrary subsets of the ball (zero cost), none of which has the form {c <= w} with w > 0. Additionally, the lemma statement omits the volume constraint |S| = v_i under which the minimization is performed (the proof imposes it); without it the minimizer is the empty set, not a sublevel set with w > 0.

failure_location.quote: there exists a unique $w^*>0$ such that $U(w^*) = v_i$

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: State the minimization among shapes of volume v_i and add the standard hypothesis that the level sets of c_i have zero Lebesgue measure (equivalently, that w -> |{c_i <= w}| is continuous); the given proof is then valid, and uniqueness of the shape (not of w) should be claimed only up to null modifications.
issues.overall_effect: The lemma's conclusion (individually optimal shapes are sublevel sets of the cost) is unsupported for general admissible costs, weakening the justification of the level-set cost construction (Eq. eq:costshape) and of the relaxation-to-preferred-shape rationale; for the concrete costs used in the paper (continuous, strictly increasing along rays, measure-zero level sets) the conclusion does hold.
issues.title: Preferred-shape lemma asserts existence and uniqueness of the level-set threshold from monotonicity alone
issues.why_classification: A local, standard regularity condition (null-measure level sets, satisfied by every cost the paper actually uses) completes the existing proof verbatim; the shape-encoding construction and all downstream uses are unaffected, so no substantive content is lost.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: We assume that the elongation range (amplitude) of the protrusion $\xi_k$ is constrained by $\xi_k\geq0$ and follows the stochastic differential equation
that is, protrusions are created randomly and naturally retract.

issues.failure_explanation: The Ornstein-Uhlenbeck equation d xi_k = -xi_k dt + dB_t^k has Gaussian transitions: explicitly xi_k(t) = e^{-t}xi_k(0) + integral_0^t e^{-(t-s)}dB_s, so for every starting value xi_k(0) >= 0 and every t > 0 the law of xi_k(t) gives strictly positive probability to negative values (from xi_k = 0, P(xi_k(t) < 0) = 1/2, and the running minimum becomes negative almost surely). The drift -xi_k alone cannot keep a continuous diffusion nonnegative (a reflection/local-time term is missing). Hence no process satisfies both the displayed SDE and the stated constraint, and whenever xi_k < 0 the perturbation f = -sum xi_k G_{theta_k} changes sign, retracting instead of extending the corresponding protrusion, contradicting the stated modeling intent that protrusions are 'created randomly and naturally retract'.

failure_location.quote:
is constrained by $\xi_k\geq0$ and follows the stochastic differential equation
\[\dd\xi_k = -\xi_k\dd t + \dd B^k_t,\]

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the amplitude equation by a nonnegative diffusion, e.g. a reflected Ornstein-Uhlenbeck process on [0, infinity) or a CIR-type equation d xi_k = (kappa - xi_k)dt + sqrt(2 xi_k)dB_t, and state which convention the implementation uses.
issues.overall_effect: The random-protrusion exploration model of Section sec:random_cost (SM Video video:protrusions) is not well defined as specified: the amplitude variables have no process satisfying both stated requirements, so the perturbed cost and the resulting exploration dynamics do not follow from the written equations.
issues.title: Protrusion-amplitude SDE is incompatible with the stated constraint xi_k >= 0
issues.why_classification: A standard local modification of a single equation (reflection or square-root diffusion) yields a well-defined model with the same operation and the same claimed behavior (random creation and retraction of protrusions); no guarantee or downstream claim is lost.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Engulfment of the orange cells inside the mass of blue cells. Parameters: $\tau=0.5$, $\alpha=\beta=0.14$, $\gamma_b=\gamma_o=1$, $\gamma_{bo}=5$, $\gamma_{ow}=30$, $\gamma_{bw}=7$, grid size $512\times512$, $\Delta t = 0.0005$.

issues.failure_explanation: The caption asserts that internalization of the orange population occurs when gamma_bo < gamma_bw - gamma_ow, while quoting parameter values gamma_bo = 5, gamma_bw = 7, gamma_ow = 30: the stated condition reads 5 < 7 - 30 = -23, which is false, so the advertised criterion is violated by the very experiment it describes (the same tensions produce engulfment of orange by blue in Fig. fig:engulfment). Within the paper's own triple-junction force balance, the two medium-involving conditions are mirror images: separation holds when gamma_bo > gamma_bw + gamma_ow (right panel, consistent: 12 > 10), and complete internalization of one population by the other holds when gamma_ow > gamma_bw + gamma_bo, i.e. gamma_bo < gamma_ow - gamma_bw, which holds for the quoted values (5 < 30 - 7 = 23). The printed inequality has gamma_bw and gamma_ow interchanged and, as written, would characterize the opposite engulfment and is unsatisfiable whenever gamma_ow > gamma_bw with positive tensions.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Correct the caption's inequality to gamma_bo < gamma_ow - gamma_bw (equivalently gamma_ow > gamma_bw + gamma_bo), which is the criterion satisfied by the caption's own values and by the engulfment parameters of Fig. fig:engulfment.
issues.overall_effect: The rule advertised for distinguishing the internalization regime from the separation regime is false as stated; applying the printed inequalities to new parameter sets would misclassify sorting outcomes. The simulations, the other two criteria (checkerboard, separation) and the engulfment experiment are unaffected.
issues.title: Internalization criterion in the sorting figure is false for the caption's own parameter values
issues.why_classification: A one-line correction of the caption's inequality, forced by the caption's own numbers and consistent with the paper's separation and engulfment parameters; no formal result, rate, or guarantee depends on it.
